objectives.text: Keep sovereignty and territorial integrity without ever choosing a patron: the official 'multi-vector' line of 2020-2030 and Tokayev's practice of being received by Putin, Xi and Trump within weeks of one another (Washington 6 Nov 2025, Moscow 11-12 Nov 2025, Tianjin Sept 2025). Territorial integrity is the one principle Astana will not trade, which is why it refused to recognise the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' in Putin's presence.

objectives.text: Keep the oil flowing and find more than one way out for it. About 80% of crude exports leave through the Russian-controlled CPC pipeline to Novorossiysk (Russian companies hold 51% of the consortium); the answers are the China pipelines, the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor (about 3 Mt in January-August 2026, +22%), and Kazakh crude to Germany by Druzhba and to Ust-Luga. paradoxes.text: The troops that saved the regime fixed the price of every later act of independence. Calling in the CSTO in January 2022 gave Tokayev control at home and Moscow a claim on him; since then each defiance (no recognition of the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics', 'not a mediator' on Ukraine) has been followed by a gesture of allegiance, up to the 'alliance' declaration of 12 Nov 2025 and the Rosatom contract of 28 May 2026. The nuclear plant is meant to cut the baseload gap, and the 2024 referendum was framed as the country's own decision; the winner is Rosatom (85% Russian financing, a 2035-36 horizon), beating the Chinese, French and Korean bids. Kazakhstan thereby adds the biggest single Russian tie of the decade to its pipeline and gas dependence on Moscow.

grand_strategy.reading:
Kazakhstan is the small-state manoeuvre between three great powers, played by a
state that is not small in size but is in leverage: its long northern border
and its pipelines belong to the neighbour it must not offend, its money
comes more and more from China and the West, and its security was lent to it by
Russia in January 2022. In Luttwak's terms Astana practises the weaker party's
relational manoeuvre: it never chooses, because each patron's offer is worth
more as long as the others are watching. The constraint that disciplines the
whole system is the 2022 debt, which is paid not in money but in language: an
'alliance' declaration (12 Nov 2025), a Russian reactor (28 May 2026), CSTO and
EAEU seats kept. Every clear no (the 'republics', the sanctions pledge, the
Kazakh language) is balanced by a visible yes. Since 2025 the structure has
thickened on all three sides at once, which is the best test of a hedge: Trump
received the five presidents and Kazakhstan joined the Abraham Accords and the
Board of Peace; Xi came to Astana and then received Tokayev in Shanghai
(16 Jul 2026); Putin returned the Moscow visit with a state visit to Astana
(27-29 May 2026). The weak point is not a patron but a place: the CPC terminal
at Novorossiysk, where Russian ownership, Western capital and Ukrainian drones
meet. Signals that are not rows: Lavrov did not attend the Moscow talks of
11-12 Nov 2025 (an unusual absence), and the Druzhba stoppage of Kazakh oil to
Germany reported for 1 May 2026 arrived while Rosatom's contract was being
finished. With the new constitution in force since 1 July 2026, the open question
is whether the system survives the man: a presidential succession in 2029 would
reopen the question of who owes what to whom.

stances.note: Aligned by treaty and by debt, with visible friction. Both sides use the word: the Moscow declaration of 12 Nov 2025 raised ties to 'comprehensive strategic partnership and alliance' and Tokayev hailed 'allied relations' again with Putin in Astana on 28 May 2026 (CSTO and EAEU co-members; the dataset floor would be plain 'ally'). The friction is on the record: Astana refused to recognise the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' in Putin's presence (June 2022), calls itself 'not a mediator' on Ukraine, and the Kremlin's levers are the CPC (80% of oil exports), the reported halt of Druzhba transit to Germany from 1 May 2026 and Russian television's attacks of 2022. The 2022 CSTO intervention is the debt that explains the instalments of loyalty (the declaration, the Rosatom plant). Trend stable rather than cooling or warming: the formal ties thickened in 2025-26 while the hedge toward Washington and Beijing thickened at the same time. Bond - affinity: Soviet history, Russian language and a 15% Russian minority, but no kinship; Russian elites' view of Kazakh statehood keeps it from kin. No asymmetry with Ukraine: Kyiv does not grade Kazakhstan an adversary.

stances.note: Largest trading partner (record USD 49bn in 2025, Tokayev to Xi in Shanghai on 16 Jul 2026, with more than USD 30bn of Chinese investment) and the host of the 2nd China-Central Asia summit (Astana, 16-18 Jun 2025, where Xi signed a treaty of permanent good-neighbourliness with the five states). The official label is 'permanent comprehensive strategic partnership' (since 2019), which is a partnership, not an alliance: no defence commitment and no CSTO-type security bind, and Beijing lost the nuclear-plant bid to Rosatom. Bond - none: pure interest, with ethnic Kazakhs in Xinjiang as a point on which Astana is silent and a public wary of Chinese presence. Two independent sources (the Chinese foreign ministry and the Kazakh government) use the 'strategic partnership' reading.

Still not an alliance: the Jackson-Vanik repeal for Kazakhstan was only a bill in July 2026, there is no defence treaty, and five days after Washington Tokayev signed the 'alliance' declaration in Moscow. Bond - none: interest only; the Abraham Accords step is Tokayev's offer for Trump's attention.

The Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement has applied since 2016 and is in force since 1 Mar 2020; the Global Gateway Investment Package for Central Asia (EUR 12bn, Samarkand, April 2025), the critical-raw-materials roadmap and Tokayev's Brussels visit (concluded 23 Jun 2026: USD 12bn of agreements including 50 Airbus aircraft for EUR 7.1bn) deepen it. Non-member, hence partner, whatever the rhetoric of strategic partnership. Friction: EU sanctions listings of Kazakh firms for Russia re-export and a visa facilitation agreement still under negotiation. Bond - none.

relations_from.summary: Astana wants a trade and transit route through Afghanistan to Pakistan, India and the Gulf: a Turgundi-Herat-Kandahar-Spin Boldak railway (protocol of intent 24 Apr 2025, about 120 km first stage, 2026-27 start planned), with the Taliban government engaged but not recognised.

sources.title: Kazakhstan and Afghanistan sign protocol of intention on railway construction
Kazakhstan outlines financing plan for Turgundi-Herat railway, eyes 2026 start

relations_from.summary: Astana wants to be the EU's partner for the Middle Corridor, critical raw materials (a 2025-26 roadmap on raw materials, batteries and green hydrogen) and uranium and oil as a replacement for Russian supply, without joining any Western bloc.

sources.title: Kazakhstan lands USD 12 billion in EU deals to expand energy and trade ties
DGAP Policy Brief No. 12: EU connectivity in Central Asia

relations_from.summary: Tokayev said at the St Petersburg forum on 17 Jun 2022, beside Putin, that Kazakhstan does not recognise the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' ('quasi-state formations'), citing the same principle as for Taiwan, Kosovo, Abkhazia and South Ossetia; the foreign ministry has not recognised the later annexations. Zelensky thanked him. Putin suspended a Kazakh oil shipment via Novorossiysk the next day (reported).

sources.title: Face to face with Putin, Kazakhstan's president refuses to recognise Ukraine breakaway republics
Ukraine war: Is Kazakhstan going cool on Russia?
Zelenskyy thanks Kazakhstan's President Tokayev for not recognising Luhansk and Donetsk 'republics'

relations_from.summary: Declaration on raising relations to 'comprehensive strategic partnership and alliance' signed in the Kremlin on 12 Nov 2025 (42 points; 14 documents; politics, security, economic integration), followed by a joint statement on 'seven pillars of friendship and good-neighbourliness' in Astana on 28 May 2026. No mutual-defence text found beyond CSTO Article 4.

sources.title: Russia, Kazakhstan sign strategic partnership declaration
Between Trump and Putin, Tokayev emerges as a regional diplomatic powerbroker
Russia signs agreement to build first nuclear power plant in Kazakhstan

relations_from.summary: Treaty on Allied Relations signed in Tashkent on 22 Dec 2022 with a border demarcation agreement; ratified by Uzbekistan on 30 Nov 2023 and by Kazakhstan on 25 Apr 2024. It covers politics, trade, transit, energy and security coordination against terrorism and extremism.

sources.title: Kazakhstan ratifies treaty on alliance relations with Uzbekistan
Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan continue to strengthen strategic tandem
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan

relations_from.summary: Permanent comprehensive strategic partnership since 2019 (after the strategic partnership of 2005 and the comprehensive one of 2011), reinforced by the treaty of permanent good-neighbourliness and friendly cooperation that Xi signed with the five Central Asian presidents at the 2nd China-Central Asia summit in Astana on 17 Jun 2025.

sources.title: Kazakhstan and China continue to strengthen their permanent comprehensive strategic partnership
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan

sources.title: Xi signs treaty to elevate China's ties with Central Asia at Astana summit

relations_from.summary: Kazakhstan acceded to the Abraham Accords, confirmed by Tokayev on 6 Nov 2025 at the C5+1 summit in Washington; no Central Asian state had previously joined a US-brokered Middle East framework. Astana keeps its support for the Palestinians and a two-state solution.

sources.title: Between Trump and Putin, Tokayev emerges as a regional diplomatic powerbroker
Tokayev praises Trump's 'common sense' governance, backs US-led peace initiatives

relations_from.summary: Declaration of Eternal Friendship and Partnership signed during Erdogan's state visit to Astana on 14 May 2026, after the 6th meeting of the Turkiye-Kazakhstan High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council; 13 agreements in all.

sources.title: Turkiye and Kazakhstan ink 13 deals during Erdogan visit
Kazakhstan to become overseas production base for Turkish ANKA drones

relations_from.summary: The Supreme Court removed the Taliban from Kazakhstan's list of banned organisations on 20 Dec 2023 (made public by Tokayev on 3 Jun 2024 as a step toward trade and economic cooperation); Astana has not formally recognised the Taliban government, and the foreign ministry cited the absence of the Taliban from the UN terrorist lists.

sources.title: Kazakhstan removes Taliban from list of banned organizations
Kazakhstan removes Taliban from banned list (Tokayev explains the decision)

relations_from.summary: As much as 80% of Kazakh oil exports leave through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium to the Russian Black Sea terminal at Novorossiysk; Russian companies hold 51% of the CPC, Kazakh 19%, US 28%. CPC was stopped twice after the invasion (2022); Moscow's levers are fees, scheduling and the terminal.

sources.title: Ukrainian attacks on the CPC oil pipeline and the outlook for Kazakhstan's oil sector
Ukraine war strains ties between Kazakhstan and Russia

relations_from.summary: Kazakh crude reaches the Schwedt refinery in Germany through Russian pipelines (more than 2.1 Mt in 2025, +44%; 2.5 Mt planned for 2026). Reuters reported on 22 Apr 2026 that Russia would halt the transit from 1 May 2026; the final state of the flow is not confirmed in the sources found, and Kazakh volumes were to be rerouted to Ust-Luga and the CPC.

sources.title: Russia set to cut Kazakh oil flows to Germany via Druzhba pipeline

relations_from.summary: The Karachaganak field has no gas-processing plant: the operator must reinject at least 40% and the rest goes to Russia's Orenburg plant under the KazRosGaz contract (Gazprom-KazMunayGas), extended to 2038 for up to 9 bcm a year; intake was suspended after a drone strike on Orenburg and resumed.

sources.title: Orenburg gas processing plant suspends intake of Kazakh gas following drone attack
Orenburg gas processing plant to supply LPG to Kazakhstan in 2024 - Kazakh Ministry of Energy

relations_from.summary: Kazakhstan's goods trade with EAEU partners was USD 30.9bn in 2025 (about 21% of USD 143.9bn total), of which Russia 88.6%; the USD 27.4bn is our arithmetic on the statistics bureau's published shares. Exports to the EAEU fell 8.3% to USD 10.1bn, imports rose 4.4% to USD 20.8bn.

sources.title: Foreign trade of the Republic of Kazakhstan, January-December 2025
sources.publisher: Bureau of National Statistics of Kazakhstan

relations_from.summary: Agreement signed on 28 May 2026 in Astana for Kazakhstan's first nuclear power plant (Ulken, Lake Balkhash; two VVER-1200 per Rosatom; commissioning about 2035-36; cost quoted between USD 15bn and 16.5bn); approved by the referendum of 6 Oct 2024 (71.12% yes). Tokayev says 177 joint projects worth almost USD 53bn are under way.

sources.title: Russia signs agreement to build first nuclear power plant in Kazakhstan
Kazakhstan referendum backs new nuclear energy

relations_from.summary: The CSTO force sent at Tokayev's request on 6 Jan 2022 numbered about 2,500, about 2,000 of them Russian, to guard strategic sites; withdrawal began on 13 Jan and was completed by 19 Jan 2022. The intervention is the debt that shapes later Kazakh choices.

sources.title: Kazakhstan: the CSTO intervenes, the protests pacified
Russia completes pullout from unrest-hit Kazakhstan
3 big things to know about the Russian-led alliance intervening in Kazakhstan

relations_from.summary: China is Kazakhstan's first trading partner: record two-way trade of about USD 49bn in 2025 (USD 43.8bn in January-November, +9.3%), and more than USD 30bn of Chinese investment in the economy, cited by Tokayev to Xi on 16 Jul 2026.

sources.title: Xi Jinping meets Tokayev in Shanghai
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China

sources.title: President Tokayev, Xi Jinping hold high-level talks in Shanghai

relations_from.summary: The oil pipelines to China will soon carry 146.6 million barrels a year, about 28% of the CPC's 527.7 million; 366,500 barrels of Kashagan crude were sent to China in December 2025. The Chinese route is the largest alternative to the Russian outlet and still a fraction of it.

sources.title: Ukrainian attacks on the CPC oil pipeline and the outlook for Kazakhstan's oil sector

relations_from.summary: Chevron holds 50% of Tengizchevroil (Exxon 25%, KazMunayGas 20%, Lukoil 5%) under a concession to 2033 that the partners want extended; the Future Growth Project, completed in 2025, added 260,000 b/d. Chevron also holds 18% of Karachaganak.

sources.title: Chevron Corp, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (Tengizchevroil)
Tengiz expansion gives Kazakh capacity a boost

relations_from.summary: Cove Capital (Cove Kaz Capital) signed the final deal on 29 Apr 2026 with state miner Tau-Ken Samruk for the Northern Katpar and Upper Kairakty tungsten projects, USD 1.1bn, Cove 70% and in control of sales; its chief said the deal keeps Chinese firms out. A US-Kazakhstan critical-minerals memorandum frames it.

sources.title: American mining entity touted by Trump seals deal with Kazakhstan
US-Kazakhstan Memorandum of Understanding on Critical Minerals Cooperation

relations_from.summary: The EU is Kazakhstan's first trade partner, 32.4% of its total trade in 2024 (about USD 50bn); exports to the EU are almost entirely oil and gas, and EU countries take about 60% of Kazakh crude and product exports.

sources.title: EU-Kazakhstan factsheet
Ukrainian attacks on the CPC oil pipeline and the outlook for Kazakhstan's oil sector

relations_from.summary: Von der Leyen announced a EUR 12bn Global Gateway Investment Package for Central Asia at the first EU-Central Asia summit in Samarkand (April 2025): transport EUR 3bn, critical raw materials EUR 2.5bn, water, energy and climate EUR 6.4bn, plus digital; EUR 10bn was pledged for the Trans-Caspian route in 2024. The figure covers the region, not Kazakhstan alone.

sources.title: DGAP Policy Brief No. 12: EU connectivity in Central Asia
Visas and Middle Corridor: Kazakhstan-EU relations gain momentum at Samarkand summit

relations_from.summary: Kazakhstan ordered three Anka-S unmanned aircraft in November 2021, agreed in May 2022 to co-produce them, and on 14 May 2026 agreed a Kazakhstan Engineering - Turkish Aerospace Industries joint venture that makes it the first foreign producer of the ANKA, covering production, repair and technology transfer.

sources.title: Turkey, Kazakhstan deepen relations in space tech, drone production
Kazakhstan to become overseas production base for Turkish ANKA drones

relations_from.summary: Kazakhstan pledged at least USD 500m for the first stage of the Turgundi-Herat railway (about 120 km), planned for 2026-2027; a Kazakh deputy prime minister visited Kabul in June 2026. Astana has not formally recognised the Taliban government. Mirrors the row in Afghanistan's own file.

sources.title: Kazakhstan to invest USD 500 million in Afghan railway project, says Taliban
Kazakhstan outlines financing plan for Turgundi-Herat railway, eyes 2026 start

relations_from.summary: Annual trade between Kazakhstan and Afghanistan has risen close to USD 1bn since the Taliban took power, a reason given for the 2023 delisting.

sources.title: Kazakhstan removes Taliban from list of banned organizations

relations_from.summary: Cargo moved on the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor) in January-August 2026, up 22% year on year against a designed capacity of 6 million tonnes; about 4 million tonnes moved in 2025. Mirrors the row in Azerbaijan's file.

sources.title: Cargo traffic via Middle Corridor exceeds 3 million tons in 8 months

relations_from.summary: Kazatomprom (about 25,800 tU in 2025, roughly 20% of world primary output) said that the route avoiding Russia, via the Caspian, Azerbaijan and Georgia, carried 58% of its uranium shipments to Western customers in the first half of 2023, with 71% expected for the year; no 2025-26 split was found.

sources.title: Kazatomprom updates on shipments and plans
Cameco, Kazatomprom release 2025 production figures

relations_from.summary: State visit of Tokayev to Moscow on 11-12 Nov 2025: two and a half hours of talks with Putin before the formal session (Lavrov absent), 14 documents and the alliance declaration; Putin then paid a state visit to Astana on 27-29 May 2026 (Rosatom agreement, EAEU Supreme Council on the 29th).

sources.title: Tokayev in Moscow: balancing friendship and strategy
Russia signs agreement to build first nuclear power plant in Kazakhstan

relations_from.summary: On 5 Jan 2022 Tokayev appealed to the CSTO under its collective-security mechanism; the alliance launched its first joint operation since 1999 on the night of 5-6 Jan, with troops arriving on 6 Jan and leaving by 19 Jan; Kazakhstan has stayed in the CSTO since.

sources.title: Kazakhstan: the CSTO intervenes, the protests pacified
CSTO begins to withdraw from Kazakhstan

relations_from.summary: Kazakh entities have been listed by the EU in Russia packages (Kazstanex and Metallstan LLP in the 16th package, 2025; further Kazakh firms in a later dual-use annex; reports of a first Kazakhstan-specific anti-circumvention measure in the 19th). Tokayev pledged compliance to Chancellor Scholz in Sept 2023; officials say sanctioned goods in Kazakh exports to Russia are under 2% and customs authorities report no re-export; Kazakhstan has not itself sanctioned Russia.

sources.title: Companies in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan included in new EU sanctions package
Kazakhstan is vulnerable to secondary sanctions
EU sanctions envoy takes on delicate 'compliance' issues on visit to Kazakhstan

relations_from.summary: Tokayev's visit to Brussels, concluded 23 Jun 2026: agreements and memoranda of over USD 12bn, 50 Airbus aircraft for EUR 7.1bn, a joint statement reaffirming a roadmap on raw materials, batteries and green hydrogen, and the Middle Corridor within Global Gateway.

sources.title: Kazakhstan lands USD 12 billion in EU deals to expand energy and trade ties

relations_from.summary: C5+1 summit at the White House on 6 Nov 2025: 29 agreements worth about USD 17bn with Kazakhstan (Boeing, John Deere USD 2.5bn, Cove tungsten) and the announcement of the Abraham Accords accession. Tokayev returned to Washington on 20 Feb 2026 for the first meeting of Trump's Board of Peace.

sources.title: First deals struck at US-Central Asia summit include Boeing aircraft, mining and agricultural machinery agreements
Kazakhstan joins Donald Trump's Board of Peace as one of 19 founding countries

relations_from.summary: Tokayev signed the Charter of the Board of Peace at Davos on 22 Jan 2026 as one of 19 founding states, thanked Trump for convening it and offered Gaza humanitarian and food-security help; he says the board complements the United Nations. Separately, a bipartisan bill to repeal Jackson-Vanik restrictions on Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan was introduced on 29 Jul 2026 and has not passed.

sources.title: Kazakhstan joins Donald Trump's Board of Peace as one of 19 founding countries
Bennet joins bipartisan legislation to repeal outdated Jackson-Vanik trade restrictions on Central Asia

relations_from.summary: Xi attended the 2nd China-Central Asia summit in Astana (16-18 Jun 2025) and met Tokayev; Tokayev met Xi in Tianjin in September 2025 and again in Shanghai on 16 Jul 2026 (World AI Conference), where bilateral cooperation agreements on trade, investment and technology were signed.

sources.title: Xi Jinping meets Tokayev in Shanghai
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China

sources.title: Xi signs treaty to elevate China's ties with Central Asia at Astana summit

relations_from.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on 29 Nov 2025 hit the oil terminal near Novorossiysk that is part of the CPC; the Kazakh foreign ministry called it an exclusively civilian facility under international law and asked Ukraine to prevent a repeat (the first serious crisis in relations); Kyiv said it targeted the aggressor, not Kazakhstan. Tankers leased by KazMunayGas were hit on 13 and 19 Jan 2026 with no official Kazakh reaction; the 2026 oil target was cut from 98 to 96 Mt.

sources.title: Ukrainian attacks on the CPC oil pipeline and the outlook for Kazakhstan's oil sector
Kazakhstan urges Ukraine to halt drone attacks after CPC terminal hit in Black Sea
Kazakhstan cuts 2026 oil production goal after Ukrainian CPC strikes

relations_from.summary: Erdogan's state visit to Astana on 14 May 2026: 13 agreements, the ANKA joint venture and the Declaration of Eternal Friendship and Partnership; the Organization of Turkic States held its 12th summit in Gabala on 7 Oct 2025 with an informal one due in Kazakhstan in 2026.

sources.title: Turkiye and Kazakhstan ink 13 deals during Erdogan visit
12th Summit of the Council of Heads of State of the Organization of Turkic States commenced in Gabala

relations_from.summary: Announced in Astana with Tokayev on 21 Oct 2025 that Azerbaijan lifted all restrictions on cargo transit to Armenia in force since the occupation; the first transit cargo was Kazakh grain (arrived in November 2025). Mirrors the row in Azerbaijan's file.

sources.title: Kazakh Grain Becomes First Transit Cargo from Azerbaijan to Armenia

relations_from.summary: Mirziyoyev came to Astana in April 2026 for the Aral Sea rescue fund meeting; Kazakhstan's foreign minister was received in Tashkent in March 2026, where the allied relations were stressed again.

sources.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan continue to strengthen strategic tandem

relations_from.summary: In June 2026 Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan agreed on water releases and electricity supplies for the 2026 irrigation season, while Bishkek keeps pressing for compensation from downstream users, which Astana and Tashkent reject.

relations_from.summary: At the Dushanbe water conference in May 2026 Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan welcomed the Bahri Tojik reservoir release deal for June-August 2026.

relations_from.summary: Pezeshkian made his first official visit to Kazakhstan on 10-11 Dec 2025; Tokayev called Iran an important and reliable partner in the Caspian region, and a USD 3bn trade goal was restated.
